clue.text: Old man's given a pound by gloomy treasurer

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, an old man
L (from Latin libra) is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
grave means solemn or gloomy

explanation.surface: An elderly man is handed a pound by a miserable keeper of the purse.
explanation.walkthrough: Francis Turner Palgrave compiled The Golden Treasury of English verse, so the 'treasurer' is the anthologist, not a keeper of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Palgrave's famous anthology is called The Golden Treasury, so a crossword can call its compiler a treasurer.

clue.text: School lesson about a good part of a book

indicators.note: about means going round, so the lesson's letters are placed around the others

parts.note: PE (physical education) is a school lesson

explanation.surface: A classroom lesson concerns a decent section of a textbook.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf or one side of a leaf in a book is called by this name.

clue.text: One could start this spell after the one in France and Switzerland

indicators.note: after places the spell's letters behind the French and Swiss pieces

parts.note: in French 'the one' is l'un, giving LUN once the apostrophe goes
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland (Confoederatio Helvetica)
a spell is a period of time, here an hour

explanation.surface: Someone might begin a magic spell following the French and Swiss example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' suggests magic but means a period; 'One' is one o'clock, when a midday meal break often begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The midday meal break commonly starts at one o'clock, which is the 'One' that could begin it.

clue.text: Here a ring was stolen in a legend, from a chap in the borders

definitions.text: Here a ring was stolen in a legend

indicators.note: in places the chap inside the borders, which surround him

parts.note: rims are edges or borders
he is a pronoun for a chap, any man

explanation.surface: A tale of a stolen ring is told about a man living near a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'The Jackdaw of Rheims' from The Ingoldsby Legends, a jackdaw steals the cardinal's ring.
explanation.definitionFit: The French cathedral city is the setting of the Ingoldsby Legends poem about a thieving jackdaw.

clue.text: Nice Mr White is after a lift, in very European form of reality

indicators.note: in puts the lift and Mr White inside the very-European pair
is after places Mr White behind the lift in the run of letters

parts.note: a raise is a lift or increase
in Nice, a French city, Mr White is Monsieur Blanc, written M Blanc

explanation.surface: A Frenchman named White chases a promotion while taking a very European view of truth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, signalling a French translation.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word means verisimilitude, the appearance of truth or likeness to the real.

clue.text: Fruit found in Portugal and a part of Sicily once

indicators.note: found in places the fruit inside the letters from Portugal and a

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal
the ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Some fruit turns up in Portugal and in a part of Sicily of old.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian region was part of the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies until Italian unification in 1861.
explanation.definitionFit: The heel-of-Italy region belonged to the Bourbon Kingdom of the Two Sicilies before 1861.

clue.text: One Charlie allowed to receive an honour, ahero in a best-selling Victorian novel

definitions.text: ahero in a best-selling Victorian novel

parts.note: un is French for one
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet
let means allowed
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to accept a decoration and becomes the hero of a popular nineteenth-century book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to receive' only joins the honour on after the other pieces; nothing is inserted.
explanation.definitionFit: Harriet Beecher Stowe's 1852 bestseller, Uncle Tom's Cabin, takes its title from this enslaved central character.

clue.text: Two French articles about Indian's first prize-winning novel

indicators.note: about means the French articles go round the extra letter

parts.note: le is a French definite article (masculine)
la is the feminine French definite article

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word Indian's

explanation.surface: A pair of French grammar words frame an Indian's debut, which won a literary award.
explanation.walkthrough: Prayaag Akbar's dystopian Indian novel won the Crossword Book Award for fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: Prayaag Akbar's 2017 dystopian book carried off India's Crossword Book Award for a debut.

clue.text: A Tyrolean resort, a very sensible choice for a youngEnglish girl's education

definitions.text: a very sensible choice for a youngEnglish girl's education

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder as printed has only one N, one fewer than the answer needs

explanation.surface: An Alpine holiday spot seems a wise pick for schooling a young English girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' is a holiday spot on the surface, but read as re-sort it is the anagram signal. The setter's fodder is one N short of the answer's ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Austen's Emma, Miss Taylor is the sensible governess who educated the young heroine before marrying Mr Weston.

clue.text: Information about western country or folk?

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
re is Latin for 'in the matter of', meaning about

explanation.surface: Someone asks for facts on a western nation or its people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'western', 'country' and 'folk' look like geography and people but are all kinds of film or music.
explanation.definitionFit: Westerns, country music and folk music are each a category or style of art.

clue.text: "The you get back from children is sixpence given as change for a sovereign" (Edith Nesbit)

definitions.text: "The you get back from children is sixpence given as change for a sovereign" (Edith Nesbit)

parts.words: "The you get back from children is sixpence given as change for a sovereign" (Edith Nesbit)
parts.note: a quotation with its key word removed: the missing noun is the love or fondness children return

explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign was a gold pound coin and sixpence a small old coin, so the return is tiny next to what is given.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word is the fondness or warmth that children give back, as Nesbit wrote.

clue.text: A widow showing fear about old service

indicators.note: about means the fear word goes round the old service

parts.note: flinching means drawing back, showing fear
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A woman who has lost her husband is shown recoiling at an outdated religious rite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' suggests a church service but is the armed service, the RAF.
explanation.definitionFit: In Dickens's Little Dorrit, Arthur Clennam's old flame is now a garrulous widow.

clue.text: Agreement with someone famously doubtful — it's about a saviour who was a leper

definitions.text: a saviour who was a leper

parts.note: the apostle Thomas doubted Christ's resurrection, hence 'doubting Thomas'
a covenant is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: A pact made with a famous doubter concerns a leper who saved others.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Donaldson's fantasy series The Chronicles of Thomas Covenant follows a leper who becomes a land's saviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Donaldson's fantasy hero, an unbelieving writer with leprosy, ends up rescuing a magical land.

clue.text: Swiss cultural historian, a fool at heart reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a berk is British slang for a fool, followed by heart

explanation.surface: A Swiss scholar of culture is said to be a fool deep down.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Burckhardt wrote The Civilization of the Renaissance in Italy; 'berk' is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob Burckhardt, of Basel, wrote the classic study of the Italian Renaissance's civilisation.

clue.text: Some recalledparts of US conspiracytheory content

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the run of letters is read backwards
some means part of, so the letters sit inside the words parts of US

explanation.surface: Some features of an American plot theory are remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Flying saucers and alien craft are staples of American conspiracy theories, such as Roswell.

clue.text: New adjudicator's embraced by matchmaker and male adulterer

parts.note: Austen's Emma is a famous (and inept) matchmaker

indicators.note: embraced by means the adjudicator sits inside the male's letters

parts.note: a boy is a male
VAR, the video assistant referee, is a recent adjudicator in football

explanation.surface: A new referee is hugged by a matchmaker and a man who cheats on his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: VAR is football's video assistant referee, introduced only recently, hence 'New'.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaubert's heroine is unfaithful to her husband Charles with Rodolphe and Léon.

clue.text: Caricatures holy work of Lewis

parts.note: to ape is to mimic, so apes are imitations or caricatures
'of God' describes something holy

explanation.surface: Lampoons of a sacred work by a writer named Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: Wyndham Lewis's 1930 satirical novel mocks the Bloomsbury set; 'Lewis' tempts toward C.S. Lewis.
explanation.definitionFit: Wyndham Lewis published this satire on London's literary circles in 1930.

clue.text: Oxford writers in a book — about 50

indicators.note: about means the book's letters go around the number

parts.note: Kings is a book of the Old Testament
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Oxford authors appear in a volume of about fifty pages.
explanation.walkthrough: The group of Oxford writers included C.S. Lewis and J.R.R. Tolkien.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien, C.S. Lewis and friends formed an informal Oxford literary circle with this name.

clue.text: Clarion asorigin of German slide instrument

indicators.note: slide suggests letters slipping out of place into a new order
origin of takes only the starting letter of German

explanation.surface: A clarion call serves as the source of a German trombone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slide' suggests a trombone, but it is the anagram signal for CLARION AS and G.
explanation.definitionFit: The English horn is a woodwind of the oboe family, pitched a fifth lower.

clue.text: Prince's companion dog, maybe given a bit of offal

parts.note: a dog is an example of a pet

indicators.note: a bit of takes just one letter, the opening of offal

explanation.surface: A dog is fed a scrap of offal by a royal's friend.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Henry IV, Peto is one of Prince Hal's tavern cronies.
explanation.definitionFit: In Henry IV, Prince Hal's drinking cronies include this follower of Falstaff.

clue.text: 100 for men in an Edmund Waller poem

definitions.text: 100 for men in an Edmund Waller poem

parts.words: 100 for men in an Edmund Waller poem
parts.note: a hundred years is a great span of life for anyone, and Waller wrote a late poem on that stage of life

explanation.walkthrough: Edmund Waller's late verses, 'Of the Last Verses in the Book', are often printed under this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching a hundred years marks the latter stage of a long life, the subject of Waller's late poem.

clue.text: One London scholar distracted a husband in a complicatedmarriage

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A London academic, one of them, is preoccupied by a husband in a messy marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Nicolson and Vita Sackville-West had an open marriage, both having same-sex affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The diplomat and diarist married Vita Sackville-West, and both partners openly had other lovers.

clue.text: Performance of football manager — one replaced by United

explanation.walkthrough: Don Revie was a famous English football manager, of Leeds United and later England.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety show of sketches and songs is a kind of stage performance.

clue.text: A PC? That's rare in a city like London

definitions.meaning: P.C. is the initials of Percival Christopher, author of Beau Geste

definitions.text: That's rare in a city like London
definitions.meaning: the tiny songbird is seldom seen in a big city, though London is full of the architect Christopher's churches

explanation.walkthrough: P.C. Wren wrote Beau Geste; 'A PC' looks like a police constable or a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: P.C. is the initials of the Beau Geste novelist; the small brown songbird keeps to gardens and hedges.

clue.text: After travelling over, I am in Santa's home town, apparently in Finland

definitions.text: Santa's home town, apparently in Finland

explanation.walkthrough: The Lapland capital, on the Arctic Circle, promotes itself as the official home of Santa Claus.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lapland capital bills itself as Father Christmas's official hometown and has a Santa Claus Village.

clue.text: Large revision for a writer of stories about young men

definitions.text: writer of stories about young men

explanation.surface: A major rewrite by an author of tales about youths.
explanation.walkthrough: Horatio Alger wrote rags-to-riches stories about poor boys rising by hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio Alger's nineteenth-century novels tell of poor boys rising to respectability.

clue.text: A prolific author is teenager's introduction to reading with fluency

indicators.note: introduction takes only the opening letter of the word teenager's

parts.note: R is one of the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic

explanation.surface: A productive writer is a teenager's way into reading easily.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Trease wrote over a hundred historical novels for young readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoffrey Trease wrote more than a hundred books, mostly historical fiction for children.

clue.text: Reached a conclusion about grade one criminal

explanation.surface: Someone settled a matter concerning a first-class crook.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle or decide jointly on something is to reach a conclusion about it.
